ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; P is at the midpoint of AB, Q is at the midpoint of BC, R is at the midpoint of CD, and S is at the midpoint of AD; T is located at the midpoint of segment RS, and the shaded region is triangle PQT. According to the specified coordinate method, because only the area ratio is sought, take A=(0,0), B=(2,0), C=(2,2), D=(0,2), and the rectangle area is 4. From the midpoint conditions, P=(1,0), Q=(2,1), R=(1,2), S=(0,1). T is the midpoint of RS, so T=((1+0)/2,(2+1)/2)=(1/2,3/2). Use the shoelace formula to find the area of triangle PQT: area=1/2|1·1+2·(3/2)+(1/2)·0 - (0·2+1·(1/2)+(3/2)·1)|=1/2|4-2|=1. Therefore the ratio of triangle PQT to the area of rectangle ABCD is 1/4.
